title: Indulgences
heading: Indulgences
summary: Explains what an indulgence is (a reduction of a priest-decreed penance, not a payment for absolution), how its price scales with the buyer's means and the length of remission, and what a character must do afterwards to gain Reputation experience and a temporary Faith Point.
quotes: The poor donate what they feel they can afford, in most cases six Mythic pennies per season, and the wealthy at least a pound per season.
related: Realms of Power: The Divine p.58 Faith Points

title: Example of Creating a Devout Character
heading: Example of Creating a Devout Character
requires: Christian character with a positive Personality Trait: Pious
summary: A worked example of assigning starting Devotion Points to saints for a pious lay character, including the extra Devotion Points a relic can grant.

title: Vigils & Fasting
heading: Vigils & Fasting
summary: Rules for spending a night in prayer (a Confidence Point at the cost of a Fatigue level) and for fasting for a season (a Petitioning bonus at the cost of constant Fatigue).
quotes: A Fatigue level is lost, and will not be recovered until the character has made up a full night's sleep, but the character gains one Confidence Point that may be spent the next day on a specified virtuous task.
A fast lasts for a season and grants a +1 noncumulative bonus to Petitioning a Saint
related: Realms of Power: The Divine p.87 Petitioning a Saint

title: Devotion
heading: Devotion
requires: Christian character with a positive Personality Trait: Pious (or the Pious Personality Flaw)
summary: Introduces Devotions to particular saints as a Divine-aligned Ability-like statistic bought with separate Devotion Points rather than ordinary experience, and gives the character-generation rule for how many Devotions and Devotion Points a pious Christian starts with.
quotes: Devotions advance as an Ability, but do not use normal, generalized Experience Points, instead relying on a dedicated form of experience points called Devotion Points.
may spend Devotion Points equal to the positive score in that trait to establish Devotions
related: Realms of Power: The Divine p.87 Invoking a saint

title: The Benefits of Devotion
heading: The Benefits of Devotion
requires: Devotion to the saint invoked
summary: A Devoted character can invoke any saint he has Devotion in; the Devotion score is added to the invocation roll. Also explains sacramentals as ordinary invocations of an appropriate saint, which avoid the unknown-saint penalty.
quotes: Communication + Charm + modifiers\* + a simple die vs. 15 + a simple die
the –15 penalty for invoking an unknown saint is not applied
related: Realms of Power: The Divine p.87 Invoking a saint

title: Relics & Devotion
heading: Relics & Devotion
requires: Possession of a relic of a saint
summary: A carried or tended relic of a saint adds to the Devotion Total when asking that saint to intercede, once a day, and also removes the unfamiliar-saint penalty.
quotes: **Relic Bonus:** (Faith Points in relic) x 2 bonus to Devotion Total

title: The Costs of Devotion
heading: The Costs of Devotion
requires: Devotion to a saint
summary: A Devoted character must observe the saint's feast day each year, losing the day for seasonal activities, and loses Devotion Points if he fails to do so.
quotes: A character failing to celebrate the festival of his saint in some manner will lose at least three Devotion Points

title: Patron Saints
heading: Patron Saints
summary: Explains who counts as a character's patron saint for invocation, and that anyone may invoke Mary or a saint whose traditional interest fits the matter at hand, with no Piety required.
related: Realms of Power: The Divine p.87 Patron saints

title: Gaining Devotion Points
heading: Gaining Devotion Points
requires: Devotion to a saint
summary: Lists the activities that earn Devotion Points in play (seasons of prayer, endowing churches, guild membership, shrine visits, sponsoring art, studying hagiographies, advancing the saint's cultus, witnessing miracles, processions, pilgrimage, visions) and the usual award for each.
quotes: Spending a season engaged in prayer and meditation at a shrine to a saint earns 5 Devotion Points.
grants a number of Devotion Points equal to the Aesthetic Quality of the final artwork
worth Devotion Points equal to Quality/2
related: Art & Academe p.123 Aesthetic Quality
City & Guild p.41 Guild membership
Lords of Men p.46 Feasting
The Church Ch.3 Petitioning the Church

title: False Devotion
heading: False Devotion
requires: Devotion to a saint
summary: Devotion can be directed at an unrecognised saint or even a mistaken entity of another realm without heresy, because dulia is not worship; true worship (latria) of anything but God is a serious sin.

title: Becoming a Saint
heading: Becoming a Saint
requires: Troupe decision; character died with the Personality Trait Pious at the required level
summary: Sets out the conditions under which a deceased character may become a genuine saint and, separately, be formally canonised by the Church, and points to the saint-design rules in Realms of Power: The Divine.
quotes: died with a Personality Trait Pious of 6 or higher
related: Realms of Power: The Divine p.60-61 Miracles
Realms of Power: The Divine p.89 Designing saints

title: The Mechanics of a Pilgrimage Story
heading: The Mechanics of a Pilgrimage Story
summary: Defines minor and major pilgrimages and a Pilgrimage Target Level for each desired outcome (gaining or losing Virtues and Flaws, removing traits, penance, miracles), plus limits on which Virtues and Flaws a pilgrimage can change.
quotes: A minor pilgrimage is one that requires a Target Level of 18 and that occurs in a single season, requiring a story.
A major pilgrimage is one that requires a Target Level of 30 and that takes multiple seasons, and possibly multiple stories, to play out.
related: Realms of Power: The Divine p.60 Miracles

title: Oppositional Elements
heading: Oppositional Elements
summary: How the storyguide builds a pilgrimage story from Oppositional Elements with assigned values that each pilgrim must personally overcome, with a table of example elements by value.
quotes: **Total of Oppositional Elements Values** = Pilgrimage Target Level
The Oppositional Elements for the pilgrimage should have total value at least equal to the Target Level of the Pilgrimage.
related: Art & Academe pp.45-51 Hazards

title: An Example of a Pilgrimage Story
heading: An Example of a Pilgrimage Story
summary: A worked example of setting Target Levels, totalling Oppositional Elements and tracking which characters overcome them on a major pilgrimage.

title: Pilgrimage & Devotion
heading: Pilgrimage & Devotion
requires: Devotion to a saint
summary: Gives the Devotion Points a Devoted character earns for pilgrimage to a saint's shrine and for further relevant sites and relics seen along the way.

title: Taking the Cross
heading: Taking the Cross
summary: Rules for a character committing to a Church-preached crusade: he gains an indulgence for outstanding penance and a temporary Faith Point, must fund his own travel and upkeep, and may at the troupe's discretion shed a Social Status Flaw.
quotes: He receives a single temporary Faith Point for the commitment
related: The Church Ch.7 Templars

title: Christian Mysticism
heading: Christian Mysticism
requires: Character aligned with the Divine realm
summary: Introduces the mystic as a personal, non-institutional path to God, distinguishes contemplative and monistic mysticism and their dangers, and states that mystics must be Divine-aligned and that their Warping takes the form of Divine Ascent.
quotes: Both forms of mysticism require the character to be aligned with the Divine realm.
related: Realms of Power: The Divine Holy Traditions

title: Experiencing Divine Ascent
heading: Experiencing Divine Ascent
requires: Divine-aligned character gaining Warping Points
summary: A Divine-aligned character who gains enough Warping Points in a single event rolls to resist Divine Ascent, and on a failure undergoes Divine Form (contemplatives) or Divine Gloom (monistics) and takes extra Warping Points equal to the margin of failure.
quotes: Presence + Concentration (or Meditation) + Stress die vs. Warping Score + Warping Points gained + True Faith Score local aura + stress die (no botch)
related: Realms of Power: The Divine p.63 Divine Ascent

title: Personality Traits, Sins, and Tempers
heading: Personality Traits, Sins, and Tempers
requires: Divine-aligned characters and mystics (Sinful Traits and Tempers)
summary: Groups Personality Traits into paired Sins and Tempers, lets a trait be annotated with its Sin or Temper, and explains that a trait's value counts negatively for the opposed one.
quotes: When dealing with opposing tempers or sins, treat the trait's value as negative.
related: Realms of Power: The Divine p.40 Sins and Tempers

title: Contemplative Mysticism
heading: Contemplative Mysticism
requires: Positive Pious Personality Trait; association with the Divine realm; no Sinful Personality Traits
summary: Describes the contemplative path of imitating Christ and sets its entry requirements: a positive Pious trait, no Sinful traits and an association with the Divine realm.
quotes: the mystic must possess a positive Pious Personality Trait score
related: Realms of Power: The Divine p.40 Sinful Personality Traits
ArM5 p.18 Changing Personality Traits

title: Divine Warping and the Contemplative Mystic
heading: Divine Warping and the Contemplative Mystic
requires: Contemplative mystic who has suffered Divine Form
summary: Summarizes the permanent changes of Divine Form for a contemplative mystic: added Magic Resistance, a Soak bonus, a Penetration bonus, extra botch dice for impious acts, automatic wounds for sin and a continuous Commanding Aura.
quotes: The character gains a Penetration Bonus equal to her Warping Score, with an additional bonus equal to her (True Faith Score multiplied by 5).
The character gains a bonus to physical Soak totals equal to the Magic Resistance Total divided by 5
related: Realms of Power: The Divine p.64 Divine Form

title: Spiritual Paths and Revelations
heading: Spiritual Paths and Revelations
requires: Contemplative mysticism
summary: A contemplative mystic gains new Virtues, Methods, Powers or Supernatural Abilities by following a Spiritual Path: a Path Total is set by the Revelation sought, reduced by the character's Pious score to a Path Target, and met by completing Quest Components of listed values.
quotes: **Path Target** = Path Total – score in Personality Trait Pious
**Total Quest Component Values** = Path Total
related: The Church Ch.2 Pilgrimages

title: Monistic Mysticism
heading: Monistic Mysticism
requires: Flaw: Visions or Major Virtue: True Faith; positive Pious trait; association with the Divine realm
summary: Describes the monistic path, its entry requirements, and its Twilight-Prone-like effect that a single Warping Point forces a test for Divine Ascent, so the mystic learns from Warping experiences rather than Spiritual Paths.
quotes: requires the mystic to possess either the Flaw Visions or the Major Virtue True Faith
related: Realms of Power: The Divine p.63 Divine Gloom

title: Advantages of Pursuing Monistic Mysticism
heading: Advantages of Pursuing Monistic Mysticism
requires: Monistic mysticism
summary: Monistic mystics gain extra experience from practising Holy Abilities (equal to Concentration) and, after Divine Ascent, may roll to integrate a Revelation and choose a benefit such as keeping mundane experience, a new Virtue, substituting Dominion Lore for another Realm Lore, or accepting the Infernal as subordinate to the Divine.
quotes: Intelligence + Concentration + stress die vs. Warping Score + stress die (no botch)
gains experience points equal to her Concentration Ability score rather than 4 experience points
related: ArM5 Wizard's Twilight

title: Divine Warping and the Monistic Mystic
heading: Divine Warping and the Monistic Mystic
requires: Monistic mystic who has suffered Divine Gloom
summary: Summarizes Divine Gloom for a monistic mystic: Warping Points convert into experience in Dominion Lore and Holy Abilities at the cost of mundane Ability experience, with a bonus against Celestial Disorientation and attraction of supernatural beings.
related: Realms of Power: The Divine p.63 Divine Gloom
Realms of Power: The Divine p.14 Celestial Disorientation

title: Improving True Faith
heading: Improving True Faith
requires: Virtue: True Faith
summary: True Faith can only be gained or raised through a story and a troupe decision, and higher scores grant extra abilities such as dispelling illusions, doubled Magic Resistance against Mentem, and an Empyreal Aura.
quotes: At True Faith 3, the character gains double Magic Resistance against Mentem spells and similar supernatural powers, and adds +6 instead of +3 to a die roll for each Faith Point spent.
related: Realms of Power: The Divine pp.56-63 True Faith
Realms of Power: The Divine p.12 Empyreal Aura

title: Clergy as Player Characters
heading: Clergy as Player Characters
summary: Clergy characters are built as ordinary grogs or companions under the standard character rules; the sidebar lists ways clergy can be tied into a covenant saga.
related: ArM5 Ch.3 Character creation

title: Vows
heading: Vows
summary: Guidance on how to represent a Church character's vows at character creation: the Monastic Vows Story Flaw only if the troupe wants vow-driven stories, a suitable Personality Flaw or Regular otherwise, or simply a note with no Virtue or Flaw.
related: ArM5 p.56 Monastic Vows

title: Faith Points
heading: Faith Points
summary: Faith Points are spent like Confidence Points for a bonus to a roll, normally one per roll; they do not regenerate on their own unless the character has True Faith.
quotes: Faith Points may be spent like Confidence Points to gain a +3 bonus to a roll, and usually a character may only spend 1 Faith Point on each roll.
related: ArM5 p.189 True Faith
Realms of Power: The Divine pp.56-60 Faith Points

title: Worship
heading: Worship
requires: Christian character with access to a chapel or church
summary: A free-season activity of fasting, prayer and meditation whose Source Quality comes from the Divine aura of the church, with experience restricted to Church Lore, Concentration, Music and Divine-aligned Abilities or Arts the character already has.
quotes: Worship has a Source Quality equal to the Divine Aura in the church.

title: Good Works
heading: Good Works
summary: A season spent on charitable deeds, which for clergy may be a non-free season, giving experience in an appropriate Ability and a Faith Point.
quotes: Good works has a Source Quality of 2 in an appropriate Ability, and the character also gains 1 Faith Point.

title: Care of Souls
heading: Care of Souls
requires: Ordained priest leading a congregation
summary: A priest spends a season preaching to his congregation on a virtue theme, giving willing parishioners a bonus to matching activities for the next year and the priest experience in Leadership, Area Lore or Church Lore; it can be replaced by the aura-tempering rules.
quotes: Care of souls has a Source Quality of 2 for the priest, in Leadership, Area Lore, or Church Lore.
related: Realms of Power: The Divine p.38 Tempering an Aura

title: Recommended and Required Virtues, Flaws, and Abilities
heading: Recommended and Required Virtues, Flaws, and Abilities
summary: A table of the Virtues and Flaws required and recommended, and the minimum Ability scores suggested, for popes, cardinals and archbishops; for bishops, abbots and senior officials; and for ordinary clergy.
quotes: Recommended Minimum Ability Scores: Artes Liberales 1, Church Lore 5, Civil and Canon Law 5, Dead Language: Latin 5, Theology 3.

title: Election of the Bishop
heading: Election of the Bishop
summary: How a bishop is elected by the cathedral canons, what candidate qualifications mean in game terms (Latin literacy and usually a positive Church reputation), and the grounds on which an election can be challenged by petition.
quotes: The bishop is elected by a simple majority, in a secret ballot, of the cathedral canons.
related: The Church Ch.3 Petitioning the Church

title: Proctors
heading: Proctors
summary: Proctors represent bishops, nobles or religious houses at the papal curia, presenting and appealing petitions, and are bound by four rules on tenure, concubinage, number per client and substitutes.
quotes: There are four rules for proctors:
related: The Church Ch.3 Petitioning the Church

title: Ordination
heading: Ordination
summary: Ordination is a seasonal activity ending in an oral examination: the Examination Total is compared with an Ease Factor set by the grade sought, with Reputation consequences for a very good or marginal result, a Faith Point on success, and appeal or petition when the exam is failed or botched.
quotes: **Ordination Examination Total:** Intelligence + (Church Lore or Civil and Canon Law) + stress die
If the character's Ordination Exam Total is more than double the required Ease Factor
misses the required Ease Factor by less than 6
related: ArM5 p.167 Reputation experience
The Church Ch.3 Petitioning the Church

title: Rapid Ordinations
heading: Rapid Ordinations
summary: A character ordained through several grades at once, for example when elected bishop, still gains only a single Faith Point from ordination.

title: Possession and Exorcism
heading: Possession and Exorcism
summary: An exorcist spends a Confidence or Faith Point and generates an Exorcism Total, which succeeds if it meets an Ease Factor equal to the Might Points the demon has invested in the possessed victim; ordination as exorcist, holy water and a crucifix add bonuses.
quotes: **Exorcism Total:** Stress Die + Bonuses
If the Exorcism Total equals or exceeds an Ease Factor equal to the number of Might Points invested in the energumen by the demon, then the demon is exorcised.
related: Realms of Power: The Infernal p.32 Possession
ArM5 p.184 Penetration

title: Canon Courts
heading: Canon Courts
summary: Explains who judges in the Church's courts, how clergy are shielded from secular justice, what falls under canon jurisdiction, how summons and judgments work, and how compurgation can acquit a defendant on character witnesses.
quotes: A person cannot be forced, except by papal decree, to attend a canon court further than two days travel from his diocese.

title: Punishment
heading: Punishment
summary: Lists the Church's punishments: excommunication, irregularity (which stops a cleric using Faith Points), monition, public penance, imprisonment in a religious house, fines and suspension of a benefice; canon courts may not impose death or physical punishment.
quotes: An irregular clergyman cannot make use of Faith Points.
An excommunicate character is cursed and receives no benefit from any of the Sacraments except penance

title: Shedding of Blood
heading: Shedding of Blood
summary: Lists what clerics are forbidden to do with regard to bloodshed, including sentencing, attending punishments, commanding fighting men and ordeals, and (for major orders) practising chirurgy.
quotes: Clerics are forbidden to shed blood.
In addition, clerics in major orders may not practice chirurgy.
related: Realms of Power: The Divine p.78 Ordeals

title: Sanctuary
heading: Sanctuary
summary: A church, churchyard and cemetery give fugitives a limited period of sanctuary during which blood may not be spilled.
quotes: Sanctuary is granted for up to 40 days

title: Simony
heading: Simony
summary: Buying or selling sacred things is a canon crime; the buyer loses what was gained and the seller is fined and may be excommunicated for repeat offences.
quotes: The seller is fined twice the value of the transaction

title: Relics
heading: Relics
summary: Summarizes how relics work: Faith Score and Faith Points, Magic Resistance for the holder, a Divine Might Score and an aura hostile to the Infernal that damages entering creatures of lesser Might.
quotes: Anyone who holds the relic has a Magic Resistance equal to 10 x the Faith Score
related: Realms of Power: The Divine pp.43-46 Relics

title: Tithes
heading: Tithes
summary: Everyone owes the Church a tenth of income, and canon courts prosecute under-payment, a risk for Hermetic covenants that evade the tithe.
quotes: In 1220, everyone tithes a tenth of their income to the Church.

title: Sorcery and Witchcraft
heading: Sorcery and Witchcraft
summary: Minor sorcery is rarely heard in canon courts and usually earns a public penance, while serious sorcery is prosecuted by secular courts with death as a possible punishment.
quotes: A typical penance involves wearing a white sheet before the congregation

title: Church Auras
heading: Church Auras
summary: Divine auras spread from the church altar as far as the bells can be heard or to the parish boundary, with the aura level depending on the type of church or distance from it, given in a table.
quotes: Divine auras radiate from the church altar for as far as the church bells can be heard, or to the edge of the parish boundary, whichever is closer.

title: Spells in Church
heading: Spells in Church
summary: For Hermetic spells, explains how a church is divided into Rooms (nave, tower floors, a petitioned-off chancel) and that the whole church can be targeted as a Structure.
quotes: For Hermetic magic, the nave and each floor of the tower count as separate Rooms.
related: ArM5 Ch.4 Target Room and Structure

title: Hermetic Magic and the Sacraments
heading: Hermetic Magic and the Sacraments
summary: Notes the observable magical effects of the Sacraments for Hermetic magic, such as baptismal names being useless as Sympathetic Connections and bodies that have received Extreme Unction being immune to magic for a time.
quotes: bodies that have received Extreme Unction cannot be affected by magic for three days

title: The Sacraments
heading: The Sacraments
summary: Treats the seven Sacraments as supernatural Divine powers that need no Penetration but require willing participants, with a Faith Point available from each and specific effects for baptism, confirmation, Mass, marriage, penance, ordination and extreme unction.
quotes: A character may not have more than 1 Faith Point from each Sacrament.
related: Realms of Power: The Divine p.74 Sacraments

title: The Benefice
heading: The Benefice
summary: Explains the benefice as the income attached to a parish, who may assign it, the legitimate reasons for a priest to be absent (study, service elsewhere, pluralism), and how licenses of absence and benefice exchanges are handled.
related: The Church Ch.3 Petitioning the Church

title: Spells to Affect a Parish
heading: Spells to Affect a Parish
summary: Gives the Boundary-target Size Modifiers needed for Hermetic spells to cover a typical rural parish, urban parish or whole diocese, provided the borders are clearly defined.
quotes: A rural parish of typical size requires a spell with a Boundary target, with a +4 Size Modifier.
related: ArM5 Ch.4 Target: Boundary

title: Visitations
heading: Visitations
requires: Bishop, archdeacon or rural dean making visitations
summary: Describes the yearly visitation of parishes by bishops and their deputies, its cost to the parish, retinue size limits by rank, and the experience a season of visitation earns the visitor and retinue.
quotes: A season spent on visitation is worth 2 exposure experience points in Church Lore, Civil and Canon Law, Area Lore, or Ride for the visitor and his retinue.

title: The Petition Total
heading: The Petition Total
summary: The core procedure for getting the Church to act: a Petition Total, built from Communication or Presence plus Church Lore plus modifiers and with no die roll, is compared with an Ease Factor set by the request, with a list of example Ease Factors and rules for who can grant what, written versus audience petitions, and scribes.
quotes: **Petition Church:** Petition Total vs Petition Ease Factor
**Written Petition Total:** Com + Church Lore + Modifiers
**Audience Petition Total:** Pre + Church Lore + Modifiers
related: The Church Ch.3 Ordination
The Church Ch.2 Furthering the cultus

title: Modifiers to the Petition Total
heading: Modifiers to the Petition Total
summary: Lists the bonuses and penalties that supporters, donations, arguments based on Abilities, visions, miracles and reputation add to a Petition Total, how an argument is rolled, and which bonuses do not stack.
quotes: **Argument Success:** Int + Ability Score + stress die vs Ease Factor of 9

title: Henri of Toulouse's Petition
heading: Henri of Toulouse's Petition
summary: A worked example of building a Petition Total for founding a monastery from a scribe's total plus several supporting modifiers.

title: The Petition of the Parish of Long Melford
heading: The Petition of the Parish of Long Melford
summary: A second worked example of a Petition Total, for moving a parish's feast days.

title: Acting Without Authority
heading: Acting Without Authority
summary: Sets the highest Ease Factor of petition that a bishop or a priest may grant on his own authority, and notes that such decisions can still be questioned later and that characters may act beyond their authority at some risk.
quotes: A bishop (or equivalently ranked character) may grant any petition or take any action with an Ease Factor of up to 15 without consulting his peers or superiors.

title: Appealing a Petition
heading: Appealing a Petition
summary: An appeal is itself a petition whose Ease Factor to overturn is based on the original Petition Total, with a compromise offered if it falls only slightly short, and a penalty for appealing after the original season.
quotes: **Ease Factor to Overturn a Petition:** Original Petition Total + 3
**Ease Factor to Open Negotiations for Compromise:** Original Petition Total – 3
If an appeal is not made in the same season as the original petition, then the appeal has a –3 penalty to its Petition Total.

title: Creating Game Statistics for a Church
heading: Creating Game Statistics for a Church
summary: Introduces describing a church with Build Points, Hooks and Boons in the same way a covenant is described, to show how the Church affects the saga.
related: ArM5 pp.68-74 Covenant creation

title: Basic Church Features
heading: Basic Church Features
summary: Explains how a church is built from Build Points, Hooks and Boons (major and minor), and gives the base Divine aura and Build Points for each kind of church from cathedral to chapel.
quotes: You may usually choose up to 10 points of Hooks for the church.
A parish church has a base Divine Aura of 4, and 250 build points.
related: ArM5 pp.72-74 Hooks and Boons

title: Resources
heading: Resources
summary: Build Point costs for a church's resources: books, enchanted items, relics priced by Faith Score and powers, specialists and vis, mostly at the same cost as for a covenant.
quotes: **Enchanted Item Cost:** 1 Build Point per Level of Effect
**Relic Cost:** Cost for Faith Score + 5 Build Points per Power
related: ArM5 pp.71-72 Covenant resources

title: Hooks and Boons
heading: Hooks and Boons
summary: Notes that most covenant Hooks and Boons from the core rules and Covenants also suit churches, with a few new church-specific ones added.
quotes: are suitable for a church, although some may require interpretation by the troupe
related: ArM5 pp.72-74 Hooks and Boons
Covenants pp.6-27 Hooks and Boons

title: Becoming a Monk or Nun
heading: Becoming a Monk or Nun
summary: The procedure for entering a religious house: harsh testing on arrival, a probationary year as a novice, the three solemn vows, and rules on oblates and the admission of girls to nunneries.
quotes: The three chief vows that are sworn as solemn oaths are for chastity, poverty, and obedience.

title: The Opus Dei, Divine Office
heading: The Opus Dei, Divine Office
summary: A timetable of the canonical hours, meals and chapter meetings in a monastery, giving the storyguide a guide to where monks are and what they are doing at any hour.
quotes: Roused from sleep by the sacristan with a bell, the monks attend the first service of the day.

title: Sign Language (Monastery)
heading: Sign Language (Monastery)
requires: Monastic or convent life
summary: A language Ability specific to a monastery or nunnery, with a fluency scale and defaults to the sign languages of related and unrelated houses at different penalties.
quotes: It defaults to an Ability in the language of other monasteries of the same order at –3

title: Monastic Roles and Positions
heading: Monastic Roles and Positions
requires: Playing a monk or nun with an office in a religious house
summary: Describes the offices of a religious house (abbot or abbess, prior, terrar, cellarer, bursar, infirmarian, sacrist, hostillar, chancellor and others) with the Abilities, Social Status Virtue and reputation suited to each, useful for building monastic characters and contacts.
quotes: She has a reputation of level 4, either good or bad, in both the local community and the Church.
related: The Church Ch.3 Senior Clergy

title: The Religious in Your Saga
heading: The Religious in Your Saga
summary: Advice on playing a monk or nun in a saga: limited free seasons outside the house, how religious roles bring them into the wider world, and the economic importance of monasteries and their hospitality to travellers.
quotes: even the most trusted monk may seem unlikely to have more than one free season outside the monastery each year

title: Female Religious in the Covenant
heading: Female Religious in the Covenant
summary: When a female religious character may live at a covenant: beguines, penitents and anchoresses need the bishop's permission, a nun needs a harder petition, episcopal visits must be managed, and vows and Flaws should reflect the character's way of life.
quotes: a Petition Ease Factor of 9 is appropriate
the Petition Ease Factor is 12
related: The Church Ch.3 Petitioning the Church
The Lion and the Lily p.106 Cunfin

title: Options for Absent Players
heading: Options for Absent Players
summary: Suggests using an enclosed religious or anchoress character for a player who cannot attend sessions, with ways of passing letters between the cell and the covenant.
